lines.text: Whose woods these are I think I know.
alternatives: F1 HOOZ wuudz (/ ˘) or HOOZ WUUDZ (/ /): foreground ownership.
F2 dheez ahr (˘ ˘) or DHEEZ ahr (/ ˘): soften “are” or emphasize “these”.
Give THINK or KNOW the chief accent: tentative knowledge or greater assurance.
lines.G: Sentence closes; the fronted clause ends after “are”.
lines.V: Flow, or pause after are ‖ before the statement of knowledge.
lines.R: Inversion + hedge: ownership comes first; “I think” qualifies certainty.

lines.text: His house is in the village though;
alternatives: F2 iz in (˘ ˘): a conversational light foot; “in” need not carry a full beat.
F1 HIZ HOWS (/ /): the owner. Give THOUGH more weight to sharpen the contrast.
lines.G: Main clause closes; the sentence continues through line 4.
lines.V: A small reset; “though” may sound like an afterthought.
lines.R: Alliteration: His / house share /h/. The owner is associated with the village.

lines.text: He will not see me stopping here
alternatives: F1–2 hee wil | NAHT SEE (˘ ˘ | / /), or hee wil | NAHT see (˘ ˘ | / ˘).
F3 MEE STAH- (/ /): emphasize who would be seen; HERE can stress the place.
lines.G: Line 4 adds the purpose of stopping →
lines.V: Carry into To watch, or briefly suspend after here.
lines.R: Internal rhyme: He / see / me share EE. will / fill links lines 3–4.

lines.text: To watch his woods fill up with snow.
alternatives: F3 FIL UP (/ /) or FIL up (/ ˘): weight the filling as well as, or more than, “up”.
F2 HIZ wuudz (/ ˘) recalls ownership; WATCH foregrounds the act of looking.
lines.V: Close the thought; stanza silence has no fixed duration.
lines.R: Alliteration: watch / woods, /w/. Snow filling the woods supplies visual imagery.

lines.text: My little horse must think it queer
alternatives: F3 MUST THINGK (/ /): strengthen the speaker’s inference about the horse.
F1 MEYE LIT- (/ /): personal attachment. The lexical stress stays on LIT-.
lines.G: “It” is explained by the following “To stop…” →
lines.V: Flow onward, or briefly suspend the horse’s imagined judgment.
lines.R: Anthropomorphism: the speaker attributes “think it queer” to the horse.

lines.text: To stop without a farmhouse near
alternatives: Same scan; emphasize STOP, with-OUT, FARM-house or NEAR.
The focus becomes the unusual stop, lack of shelter, human habitation or proximity.
lines.G: The stopping gains circumstances; location follows →
lines.V: Flow into Between, or lightly separate the added setting.
lines.R: Contrast develops: an expected farmhouse is absent from this stopping place.

lines.text: Between the woods and frozen lake
alternatives: Same scan; weight WOODS and LAKE equally to balance the two boundaries.
Or give FRO-zen the chief accent, foregrounding the condition of the landscape.
lines.G: The place phrase ends; the time phrase follows →
lines.V: Possible caesura after woods ‖; a small reset before line 8.
lines.R: Spatial and visual imagery: woods / frozen lake place the speaker between landmarks.

lines.text: The darkest evening of the year.
alternatives: F3 ning uhv (˘ ˘) is natural speech; ning UV (˘ /) gives “of” a light metrical lift.
Keep EEV-ning at two syllables. The expected third beat can remain lightly voiced.
lines.G: Time phrase and the four-line sentence close.
lines.V: Close or linger on year. Do not add a syllable to evening.
lines.R: Superlative: “darkest” intensifies the setting; it does not by itself establish hyperbole.

lines.text: He gives his harness bells a shake
alternatives: F1 HEE givz (/ ˘): foreground the horse as the acting subject.
Or let hee givz (˘ ˘) pass lightly, with BELLS and SHAKE carrying the action.
lines.G: Main-clause core; the attributed purpose follows →
lines.V: Flow into To ask, or briefly let the bell action register.
lines.R: Auditory imagery: harness bells interrupt the scene. he / his / harness echo /h/.

lines.text: To ask if there is some mistake.
alternatives: F2–3 if dhair | iz suhm (˘ ˘ | ˘ ˘): conversationally light between ASK and TAKE.
SOME can imply an unspecified error; F3 IZ suhm (/ ˘) asks whether one exists.
lines.G: The purpose and indirect question close the sentence.
lines.V: A completed thought; no direct question mark is printed.
lines.R: Personification: “To ask” turns the bell shake into a practical objection.

lines.text: The only other sound’s the sweep
alternatives: Same scan; emphasize ON-ly for exclusion, OTH-er for contrast, or SWEEP for motion.
sound’s = sound is, contracted to one syllable: SOWNDZ.
lines.P: apostrophe in sound’s; no end mark
lines.V: Carry sweep into Of; a suspension must preserve their link.
lines.R: Alliteration + sibilance: sound’s / sweep repeat /s/; /z/ adds a voiced hiss.

lines.text: Of easy wind and downy flake.
alternatives: Same scan; weight WIND and FLAKE to identify the sources of the sound.
Or weight EA-sy and DOWN-y to foreground gentleness and softness.
lines.V: A gentle or distinct close; whispering is a reader’s choice.
lines.R: Metaphorical, tactile imagery: “downy” likens the flake’s softness to down feathers.

lines.text: The woods are lovely, dark and deep,
alternatives: Same scan; let LOVE-ly govern the description, with “dark and deep” elaborating it.
Or give all three adjectives comparable force. A pause after lovely falls inside F3.
lines.G: Description ends; But introduces a counterstatement →
lines.V: lovely ‖ dark is optional; the endpoint pause may be light or strong.
lines.R: Three-part description: lovely, dark, deep; dark / deep alliterate on /d/.

lines.text: But I have promises to keep,
alternatives: F1 BUT eye (/ ˘) sharpens the turn; BUT EYE (/ /) also foregrounds the speaker.
F2 HAV PRAH- (/ /) stresses obligation. Keep F3 mi-siz light (˘ ˘).
A four-beat recitation can preserve timing without moving the stress off PRAH-.
lines.G: “I have” also governs the following “miles…” phrases →
lines.V: Light pause, or continue to let obligations accumulate.
lines.R: Turn / antithesis at But. Parallel noun + infinitive: promises to keep / miles to go.

lines.text: And miles to go before I sleep,
alternatives: Same scan; MILES / GO / be-FORE / SLEEP shift the focus: distance / action / order / rest.
F1 AND MEYELZ (/ /) adds insistence; AND is the full form of weak uhnd.
lines.G: The miles-phrase ends and is immediately repeated →
lines.V: Optional pause after go ‖; a short or long gap before line 16.
lines.R: Anaphoric opening + repeated ending begin the final pair. go recalls rhyme family A.

lines.text: And miles to go before I sleep.
alternatives: Keep the same scan, or choose any of line 15’s emphasis variants.
Renewed resolve, weary repetition, plain restatement or reflective slowing are possible.
lines.G: Repeated phrase and the entire sentence close.
lines.V: Firm fall, fading weariness or reflective slowing; none is compulsory.
lines.R: Immediate full-line repetition (epizeuxis); identical sleep / sleep inside monorhyme.
